chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, accepts from him even a single salat (prayer), He will not punish him; and whoever He accepts from him a good deed, He will not punish him.

key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the One who accepts deeds and judges His servants
key_terms.حَسَنَةً: a good deed performed in obedience to Allah
key_terms.صَلَاةً: salat (prayer), the ritual act of worship
key_terms.قَبِلَ: accepted; indicating divine acceptance of an act
key_terms.وَاحِدَةً: a single one; emphasizing even one accepted prayer
key_terms.يُعَذِّبْهُ: punishes him; refers to divine punishment

ai.seo_question: What does it mean if Allah accepts even one prayer or one good deed from a person?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the immense value of divine acceptance of deeds, especially salat (prayer). Its focus is not merely on performing acts, but on Allah’s acceptance of them, which signifies salvation from punishment.
